title: Holocaust survivor, 90, dies nearly a year being wounded in mass shooting at Australian Hanukkah event
summary: A 90-year-old Holocaust survivor has died almost a year after she was wounded during the massacre of 15 people at a Sydney Hanukkah celebration, officials said Friday.

image.caption: People visit a floral tribute outside the Bondi Pavilion on Dec. 19, 2025, several days after the deadly mass shooting at Sydney's Bondi Beach, which occurred during a Hannukah-related event. (Steve Markham/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: World·New
A 90-year-old Holocaust survivor has died almost a year after she was wounded during the massacre of 15 people at a Sydney Hanukkah celebration, officials said Friday.
Not clear yet if Eva Geller's death will lead to modified charges for 25-year-old charged in mass attack
Romanian-born Eva Geller died Thursday night in a Sydney hospital, Executive Council of Australian Jewry director Evan Zlatkis said.
She was one of around 40 people wounded when two gunmen allegedly inspired by the Islamic State group opened fire on a crowd at Bondi Beach on Dec. 14. Fifteen victims aged 10 to 87 died.
Rabbi Aron Moss said Geller had been "strong and pretty healthy right up until the Bondi attack where she was shot."
She had been admitted to the hospital several times in recent weeks due to surgery complications, Moss said.
"She's a proud mother, grandmother and great-grandmother. A beautiful, positive person who even in these difficult months maintained her positivity," Moss said on the family's behalf.
"She was told after being shot that she will never walk again by the doctors. But through sheer determination, she got back up and she did walk again," Moss added.
She walked with a cane following the leg wound, he said.

A life marked by unimaginable suffering, extraordinary strength and resilience. We mourn the passing of Eva Geller, Holocaust survivor and the 16th victim of the Bondi Beach terror attack. May Eva's memory be a blessing. 🕯️ Shabbat Shalom. https://t.co/YWeqsxnIOD—AIJAC_Update
State Premier Chris Minns offered his condolences to Geller's family.
"After everything Geller endured, the news of her death is heartbreaking," Minns said in a statement.
"Almost a year on, we are still living with the pain and aftershock of that evil act. We will never forget Eva or any victim whose life was changed forever," Minns added.
Coroner expected to rule on cause of death
Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said the devastation of the Bondi attack continued to cause pain for families.
"Eva should have been able to celebrate Hanukkah in peace and safety and, instead, her life was changed forever by an act of terror and antisemitism," Albanese said in a statement.
The surviving gunman, Naveed Akram, has been charged with 15 counts of murder, 43 of attempted murder and one of committing a terrorist act. He has yet to enter a plea.
It was not yet clear whether Geller's death would change the charges the 25-year-old Akram faces.
Who is the Bondi Beach hero?
Police said in a statement they were awaiting advice from a state coroner, who would investigate the circumstances of her death.
Akram is next scheduled to appear in court on Feb. 24, when prosecutors expect to finalize what charges will go to the New South Wales state Supreme Court for trial.
Sajid Akram, his father and also a gunman in the attack, was shot dead by police at the scene on Dec. 14, 2025.
